items.title: Bobby Johnson Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: he was one of the ones who taught me how to play and how to act and all that kind of stuff.

ctx.x: Yes. Well he was in “The Benny Goodman Story” with the Louis Armstrong band. As a matter of fact he was one of the ones who taught me how to play and how to act and all that kind of stuff. So I always wanted to be a singer and a trumpet player. There used to be, at twelve o’clock every day all over the country, there was a band called The Claude Hopkins Orchestra. And they came from the Roseland Ballroom at twelve o’clock. Now this was during the days when they didn’t have that many radio stations you know. Like…

“It’s twelve noon on Broadway,” and then you would hear Ovie Alston saying, “I will swim the ocean wide/I will take that great big ride.” And man I used to go crazy. I’d say this has got to be one of the days.
